decisions.evidence: Round 1 specification presentation; Round 1 client: “the spec says it'll just use the raw web address as the title and that it deliberately won't fetch anything” and requests “automatically pull in the page's name (and a short description).” Round 2 maker presents the corrected retrieval behavior, which the client approves.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the initial decision not to retrieve metadata contradicted automatic title/description collection. The client supplied the conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client explicitly limits the expected retrieval to “just the basic title/description”; Round 2 maker specifies only “page-title and description retrieval,” and the Round 2 client says this is “exactly what I was asking for.”
decisions.note: The revised specification omits the required favicon and preview image. The client explicitly states and accepts a narrower metadata expectation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client: “I don't need saved copies of pages”; Round 2 maker: “No generated summaries or saved page copies—only published page metadata”; Round 2 client approves the revision as exactly requested.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client explicitly accepts omission of local and Internet Archive page snapshots.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “import/export … are excluded.” Round 1 client broadly says “Everything else you've described is what I want” without identifying import as a reference difference.
decisions.note: Netscape HTML import was explicitly excluded. The blanket approval does not qualify as an explicit accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “import/export … are excluded.” Round 1 client broadly says “Everything else you've described is what I want” without identifying export as a reference difference.
decisions.note: Netscape HTML export was explicitly excluded. The blanket approval does not demonstrate that the client surfaced the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents a library “supporting save”; Round 1 client confirms “saving … [is] all there.”
decisions.note: The specification records URL-based bookmark saving, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker requires “Editable auto-filled values”; Round 2 client confirms “I can still edit them.”
decisions.note: The revised specification makes collected title and description editable.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “confirmed deletion”; Round 1 client confirms “delete-with-confirmation” is present.
decisions.note: Deletion is a recorded conforming specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents support for “tags”; Round 1 client confirms “tagging” is present.
decisions.note: The recorded tagging decision conforms to assigning tags to bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “sorting”; Round 1 client confirms sorting is included.
decisions.note: The specification records list sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “archiving, restoring, and confirmed deletion”; Round 1 client explicitly approves “archiving with restore, and delete-with-confirmation.”
decisions.note: Archive is reversible and presented distinctly from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker says the MVP delivers “reopening links”; Round 4 client confirms the tasks cover “opening links.”
decisions.note: The task-stage decision to open saved links conforms to navigation to the original URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker implements “Automatic editable title and description retrieval.” Round 5 client explicitly evaluates “the automatic page details we agreed on” and accepts the application as exactly wanted; the earlier Round 1 expectation was “just the basic title/description.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, retrieval still omits favicon and preview image. The client's explicit narrower metadata expectation and final acceptance establish an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents persistent bookmarks; Round 5 client reports “Saving a link works and it sticks around after reloading.”
decisions.note: The implemented save behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents “Automatic editable title and description retrieval”; Round 5 client confirms “I can fill in a title [and] description” and that later editing updates the entry.
decisions.note: Collected metadata remains editable in the implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 running application presentation; Round 5 client reports that pasting the same link “warns me and points me to the one I already saved instead of duplicating it.”
decisions.note: The tested implementation converges duplicate saves on the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents persistent tags; Round 5 client confirms “I can fill in … tags.”
decisions.note: Implemented tag assignment conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents filtering; Round 5 client reports “filtering by tag … works.”
decisions.note: The implementation supports filtering to a selected tag.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents search; Round 5 client reports that it finds links by “title, address, description … regardless of capitalization.”
decisions.note: The recorded implementation decision conforms for the explicitly presented full-text fields and case-insensitive matching.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents sorting; Round 5 client confirms “newest, oldest, and A–Z all behave.”
decisions.note: Multiple implemented sort keys conform to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents “confirmed deletion”; Round 5 client reports that deleting “removes it for good from both views.”
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark deletion is implemented.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents archiving; Round 5 client reports that “archiving moves it out of the main list.”
decisions.note: The recorded archive behavior hides archived bookmarks from the default list while retaining them.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents archiving, restoring, and deletion; Round 5 client distinguishes restoration—“brings it back untouched”—from deletion, which “removes it for good.”
decisions.note: The implementation clearly distinguishes reversible archive from permanent delete.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents archiving and restoring; Round 5 client reports that archived entries move “into the Archive” and deletion removes entries “from both views.”
decisions.note: A separate archive view is recorded and tested.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker generically presents “editing,” and Round 5 maker again says “Editing”; the Round 5 client only says “Editing updates the entry” without identifying whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable.
decisions.note: Across specification and implementation review, editing is presented too generically to establish conformity or divergence for the complete reference field set.
